title: Oklahoma 18, Florida State 17: The 1981 Orange Bowl Two-Point Win
question: Who caught the two-point conversion that won the 1981 Orange Bowl for Oklahoma?
answer: Tight end Forrest Valora caught J.C. Watts's two-point pass in the final two minutes, giving Oklahoma an 18-17 win over No. 2 Florida State in the January 1, 1981 Orange Bowl.
summary: Down 17-10 late, OU ditched the wishbone, scored on a Watts pass to Steve Rhodes, then went for two. Forrest Valora's catch beat No. 2 Florida State 18-17.
body: For most of the night of January 1, 1981, the Orange Bowl belonged to Florida State. The second-ranked Seminoles' defense had kept No. 4 Oklahoma's wishbone in check, and the Sooners trailed 17-10 when they got the ball back at their own 22 with 3:19 to play.

So Barry Switzer's run-first team went to the air. Quarterback J.C. Watts completed four passes on a nine-play, 78-yard drive and finished it with an 11-yard touchdown throw to split end Steve Rhodes. That made it 17-16.
Oklahoma didn't settle for the tie. On the two-point try, Watts sprinted right and lofted the ball to tight end Forrest Valora, who was alone in the end zone. The Sooners led 18-17.

Florida State drove to the OU 45, and with five seconds left kicker Bill Capece tried a 62-yard field goal. It came up short, and Oklahoma had its third straight Orange Bowl win. Watts was named the game's MVP for the second year in a row.
Watts, who later represented Oklahoma in Congress, told News On 6 in 2001 that the conversion launched his career.
